rv.q: From start to finish, the show is a joy: a love song to the exhilaration, pain and giddy nonsense of passion, with Tom Hiddleston and Hayley Atwell absolutely acing it at the helm.
The plaudits for this show will continue to echo long after its too-short run has concluded.
Lloyd’s mischievous club-culture reinvention of About Nothing has colour, passion and, in the form of Tom Hiddleston, a head-miked leading man who is absolutely in command.

And we get that in a superior second half, driven by the saddening Hero subplot. Atwell finds her mojo by playing it straighter. Hiddleston allows sincerity and even vulnerability into his routine, and his natural good timing has room to breathe.
The production is big, broad and for all its contemporary trimmings, absolutely Shakespearean in the way that it welcomes everyone into the entertainment.
Jamie Lloyd’s About Nothing is a daring and inventive production that showcases Shakespeare through a modern lens.
